_notes.pages: This book has only THREE distinct content lexemes across all 5 pages (pup, mud, sit -- even sparser than dp-the-cat-sat's cat/sat/on/cats/tip-top), so getting 5 genuinely distinct cards required the same kind of deliberate, documented deviation dp-the-cat-sat's _notes describes for its page 4. p1 'pup' and p2 'mud' are each that page's first-appearance content word, straightforward. p3 ('Mud, mud, mud!') introduces no new vocabulary at all -- it is pure repetition for comic intensity (the art prompt: 'mud flying everywhere in cartoon splats filling the frame'), so rather than default to a duplicate 'mud' card (flat, non-distinct, and would collide with page 2's card), 'muddy' was used: a plain morphological derivative of the page's own repeated word 'mud', naming exactly what the picture shows (the pup at peak muddiness) without inventing an unrelated word. p4 ('The pup is a mud pup.') uses the literal two-word phrase 'mud pup' printed verbatim in that sentence -- the moment the character's name becomes true, matching the art (a walking mud-monster). p5 keeps 'sit', the book's own shouted command word and title's finale beat, mirroring how dp-the-cat-sat reserved its most distinctive word ('tip-top') for the last page.
_notes.sequencingDisplayOrder_matchDisplayOrder: Two different full derangements of [1,2,3,4,5] (no page's `order` value sits in its own position in either list): seq=[2,3,4,5,1] (cyclic shift by 1) vs identity [1,2,3,4,5] differs at every index; match=[3,4,5,1,2] (cyclic shift by 2) vs identity differs at every index; seq vs match also differ at every index (2/3, 3/4, 4/5, 5/1, 1/2) -- so neither work sheet lets a row answer itself and rebuilds stay deterministic, per README.md step 2.
_notes.yesno: 10 items (5 true, 5 false) per the dp-the-cat-sat convention. 5 true items are drawn straight from the book's own 5 pages (imageArt = p1.jpg..p5.jpg), one question per page, worded to describe exactly what that page's picture shows (single clean pup / pup sitting in a mud puddle / pup rolling, covered in mud / pup as a walking mud-monster / muddy pup sitting on command) so a teacher can visually verify book fidelity. 5 false items reuse a plain 'is/did the X ...?' phrasing keyed to this book's own actions (in mud / a mud pup / sit) on animals that never appear in mud-pup (tiger, elephant, zebra, penguin, dinosaur) -- clearly false since the book's only character is a single puppy -- via imageWord -> docs/picture-bank/photos/<word>/<word>.jpg (all 5 files verified present on disk before writing this JSON: tiger/tiger.jpg, elephant/elephant.jpg, zebra/zebra.jpg, penguin/penguin.jpg, dinosaur/dinosaur.jpg). Per the 2026-07-30 ruling, false-item words are NOT restricted to prior-week vocabulary -- picked for clear falseness relative to this specific book instead.
